title: Q-Block Computing Establishes Ottawa Headquarters to Expand Quantum Hardware R&D - Quantum Computing Report
author: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
text:
Canadian quantum systems developer Q-Block Computing has established its corporate headquarters in Ottawa, acquiring an operational facility at 20 Colonnade Road. The expansion centralizes the company’s research programs, optical and systems engineering, and administrative operations in proximity to federal defense and research institutions, while maintaining existing manufacturing and assembly facilities in Alberta.

Q-Block develops deployable hardware based on atomic and photonic modalities across three designated platforms: AllanQ for precision timing and frequency standards in GNSS-denied environments, LuciaQ for secure photonic networking, and PolarisQ for quantum information processing. The systems target operational integration across defense, telecommunications security, and critical infrastructure.

The Ottawa facility establishes an operational structure connecting prototype design and software development in Ontario with device fabrication lines in Alberta. Alongside the physical site opening, Q-Block has opened technical recruitment across quantum physics, digital-analog electrical design, FPGA development, and photonic packaging.

Official release details are available via the Q-Block Announcement here and the Q-Block Career Portal here.
